answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can tie each identity to a long, verifiable thread of completed work: reputation earned job by job, not bought in bulk. A fresh account starts as a zephyr - light, unproven, capped at tiny stakes - and only gains weight as its thread lengthens with attested deliveries. Attackers face a spiral of rising cost: every fake identity must redo months of real work to matter, while honest agents compound trust cheaply. Cheap to join, expensive to fake.
